_purpose: Anti-hallucination anchor. ONLY verified facts (confirmed by reading source in this repo, running a command, or a web search with citation). Never add an unverified claim. Assumptions do NOT belong here.

project.scope: SDK-FREE discovery only: Epson (ENPC/UDP + GS I), Sunmi (NsdManager/mDNS), Zebra (UDP-4201), SNMP brands = Star/Bixolon/Citizen/Brother/Seiko-RP (TCP-9100 sweep + SNMP identity), generic IP (TCP-9100 sweep, SNMP-enriched), USB (UsbManager). PRINTING for any brand + Seiko SLP720/721RT label printers still EXCLUDED (need proprietary jars). See decisions D1 + D5 + D7 + D8.
project.provenance: Clean-room port of the native search code in foodhub-printer-package (IPScanner.kt, EpsonUdpDiscovery.kt, EpsonPrinterHelper.kt, UsbUniversalSearch.kt, PrintUtils.kt, PermissionUtils.kt).

enpc_VERIFIED_in_source_repo.note: Verified on real TM-m30III hardware in the SOURCE repo (docs/EPSON_PRINTER_CHANGES.md comments, dated 2026-07-02). NOT re-verified on hardware in THIS repo.
enpc_VERIFIED_in_source_repo.query_fn0: ASCII 'EPSONQ' + fn(0x00) LE + 0x10 00 00 00 00 00 -> reply carries MAC at byte offset 54 (6 bytes)
enpc_VERIFIED_in_source_repo.query_fn2: fn(0x02) -> IEEE-1284 ID string (MFG/CMD/MDL...) -> model from MDL: token
enpc_VERIFIED_in_source_repo.caveat: MAC offset 54 verified for TM-m30III only; other TM models guarded (invalid MAC -> empty, IP still returned).

escpos_gs_i_VERIFIED_in_source_repo.GS_I_maker_66: bytes 1D 49 42 -> printable reply contains 'EPSON' => brand match
escpos_gs_i_VERIFIED_in_source_repo.GS_I_serial_68: bytes 1D 49 44 -> reply '_<serial>\0'; strip non-printable + leading underscore; unique id on Android 11+
escpos_gs_i_VERIFIED_in_source_repo.caveat: Epson accepts ~one concurrent TCP-9100 connection, so the serial probe often fails during search; the ENPC UDP MAC is the PRIMARY identifier, serial is BACKUP.

usb_VERIFIED.printerClass: android.hardware.usb.UsbConstants.USB_CLASS_PRINTER (0x07) on any interface => treat as printer
usb_VERIFIED.runtime_permission: NOT needed to LIST/search USB printers (UsbPrinterScanner.listConnectedPrinters works permission-free). Runtime permission is only needed to OPEN/print to a device (UsbPermissionHelper.ensurePermission).
usb_VERIFIED.permission_flags_CORRECT_for_android14: Researched (ESCPOS-ThermalPrinter #530, the real Android-14 case): Android 14 (U, API 34) FORBIDS PendingIntent.FLAG_MUTABLE with an IMPLICIT intent (crashes). Correct pattern = EXPLICIT intent via setPackage + FLAG_IMMUTABLE (+ FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT) on API 31+, and RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED on API 33+. UsbPermissionHelper already did explicit-intent + IMMUTABLE + RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED; added FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT. (Earlier belief that USB needs FLAG_MUTABLE was WRONG — corrected by research; MUTABLE+implicit is exactly what breaks on 14.) No Android 15/API 35 USB-permission change found.
usb_VERIFIED.manifest: Library manifest declares INTERNET, ACCESS_WIFI_STATE, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE + uses-feature android.hardware.usb.host(required=false); all merge into consumer apps (VERIFIED in merged example manifest).

sunmi_VERIFIED_by_decompiling_sdk.identity: serial via GS I 68 (1D 49 44) over TCP-9100 — VERIFIED from foodhub EscPosPrinterCommands.java:832 (customQuerySn == GS_I_SERIAL); implemented via EscPosSerialProbe wired into SunmiDiscovery.enrichIdentity. MAC = best-effort ARP (<=Android9 only). mDNS itself does not expose MAC/serial.

multibrand_snmp_and_zebra.note: Star/Bixolon/Citizen/Brother/Seiko discovery generalized onto ONE brand-agnostic SNMP flow (network/snmp/), + Zebra via UDP-4201 (network/zebra/). Decision D8, 2026-07-16.
multibrand_snmp_and_zebra.snmp_flow: TCP-9100 /24 sweep (NetworkScanner) -> per-host SnmpIdentityProbe. Brand from sysDescr/hrDeviceDescr token map (SnmpIdentityProbe.BRAND_TOKENS). Fields from standard OIDs: sysDescr 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0, hrDeviceDescr 1.3.6.1.2.1.25.3.2.1.3.1, prtGeneralSerialNumber 1.3.6.1.2.1.43.5.1.1.17.1, ifPhysAddress 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.6.1 (MAC). snmpOnly flag: true=only SNMP responders (discoverSnmpPrinters), false=all reachable incl GENERIC IP-only (discoverNetworkPrinters).
multibrand_snmp_and_zebra.escpos_serial_fallback_ONDEVICE: ON-DEVICE finding (V3_MIX POS terminal, 2026-07-17): MAC is NOT obtained for Star or Sunmi (ARP blocked on Android 11+; SNMP ifPhysAddress not answered). Serial via ESC/POS GS I 68 (1D 49 44) DOES work (confirmed for Sunmi + Epson). FIX: SnmpDiscovery now falls back to EscPosSerialProbe.querySerial over TCP-9100 when the SNMP serial OID is empty (covers Star + generic). Sunmi flow already used it; Epson uses EpsonTcpProbe GS I. So serial is the unique identifier for MAC-less printers. VERIFIED build+tests (16, 0 fail); on-device serial values NOT yet re-captured after this fix.
multibrand_snmp_and_zebra.zebra_flow: UDP-4201 broadcast. Request 2E 2C 3A 01 00 00. Reply header 3A 2C 2E + 0x03; fields NUL-terminated ASCII at model@0x0C, serial@0x38, hostname@0x54; IP from packet source; NO MAC in packet (MAC via SNMP enrichment). Mirrors EpsonUdpDiscovery (MulticastLock, bcast+subnet-bcast, 1s resend).
multibrand_snmp_and_zebra.pen_matching_PRIMARY: sysObjectID (1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.0) enterprise-number match is the PRIMARY brand discriminator (Snmp.oidOf + SnmpIdentityProbe.matchByPen/PEN_BRANDS), sysDescr token map is the FALLBACK. PENs VERIFIED via IANA registry/oidref/real captures: Zebra=10642, Brother=2435, Seiko-Epson=1248, Seiko-Instruments(SII)=263. Real Zebra sysDescr captured: 'Zebra Technologies ZD421-203dpi / internal wired' (token ZEBRA matches) + enterprise 1.3.6.1.4.1.10642. Brother dedicated serial OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.2435.2.3.9.4.2.1.5.5.1 (brInfoSerialNumber) NOW WIRED as a Brother-only fallback when the standard prtGeneralSerialNumber is empty.
multibrand_snmp_and_zebra.pens_NOT_IN_IANA: Star Micronics, Bixolon, Citizen do NOT appear in the IANA PEN registry (checked directly 2026-07-16) — likely no assigned PEN, so PEN matching can NEVER identify them; they rely SOLELY on the sysDescr token fallback (a real ceiling, not a fixable gap). The IANA '308 Star Technologies / 309 Micronics Computers' entries are DIFFERENT companies — do NOT use.
multibrand_snmp_and_zebra.zebra_second_pen: Zebra ALSO matches PEN 683 (ZebraNet/Eltron print servers) per LibreNMS ESI-MIB detection — added to PEN_BRANDS alongside 10642. So Zebra is covered by 10642 + 683 + sysDescr token + UDP-4201.
multibrand_snmp_and_zebra.future_discovery_leads_UNIMPLEMENTED: (1) BIXOLON has its OWN UDP discovery on ports 3337 + 9000 (per official Net Configuration Tool manual v4.18) — a positive-ID path like Epson ENPC / Zebra 4201, BUT the request/response packet format is NOT documented; do NOT ship guessed bytes (needs a capture). (2) STAR Micronics printers support mDNS/Bonjour (UDP 5353) and StarIO SMPort does discovery — likely discoverable via NsdManager like Sunmi, BUT the exact DNS-SD service type is unconfirmed. Both would raise Bixolon/Star from token-only to positively-identified once a capture/service-type is obtained.
multibrand_snmp_and_zebra.brand_tokens_ASSUMED: sysDescr fallback tokens: EPSON; STAR; ZEBRA/ZTC/ZBR (ZEBRA corroborated by real capture); BIXOLON/BXL; CITIZEN/CBM; BROTHER; SEIKO/SII/RP-E/RP-D/RP-F. Tokens + Zebra UDP offsets/request bytes are ASSUMED (researched, not hardware-verified). All centralized + overridable.
multibrand_snmp_and_zebra.snmp_default_community: 'public', read-only, enabled-by-default is the confirmed general printer norm (PaperCut/HP/Xerox docs); Bixolon POS printers ship SNMP per their Network Connection Manual. Per-brand default NOT individually hardware-confirmed.
multibrand_snmp_and_zebra.verified: COMPILE ONLY + logic: BUILD SUCCESSFUL (lib + example assembleDebug); testDebugUnitTest tests=13 failures=0 (SnmpTest 6 incl oidOf, SnmpIdentityProbeTest 5 incl matchByPen, ZebraUdpParseTest 2). NO real Star/Zebra/Bixolon/Citizen/Brother printer tested.

seiko_rp_via_snmp.note: Seiko RP-series receipt printers (RP-E10/E11, RP-D10, RP-F10) added SDK-free via SNMP (decision D7, 2026-07-16). Discovery = TCP-9100 /24 sweep (NetworkScanner) -> per-host SNMPv1 GET on UDP/161 for identity. SNMP GET/response is a hand-rolled BER codec (network/seiko/Snmp.kt), no snmp4j.
seiko_rp_via_snmp.mechanism: raw DatagramSocket UDP/161, SNMPv1, community 'public' (default, overridable).
seiko_rp_via_snmp.brand_tokens_ASSUMED: sysDescr/hrDeviceDescr matched against SEIKO/SII/RP-E/RP-D/RP-F (uppercased). These + the serial OID contents + that SNMP is enabled with community 'public' are ASSUMED pending a real-device capture. The OIDs themselves are standard RFC 1213/2790/3805.
seiko_rp_via_snmp.verified: COMPILE ONLY: BUILD SUCCESSFUL (:universal-printer-search:assembleDebug + :example:assembleDebug); SnmpTest tests=5 failures=0 errors=0 (encode matches hand-computed bytes; decode extracts serial/MAC; error-status + noSuchInstance -> null). NOT run against real RP hardware.
seiko_rp_via_snmp.scope: RP-series only. Seiko SLP720/721RT LABEL printers remain OUT (ESC/POS over 9100 but original app used the proprietary Sii SDK; no SDK-free serial/MAC path found; hardware serial only via front-panel button combo).
